meta.voice: Computational social scientist with k-punk editorial sensibility. Precise, institutional, analytically cold, but willing to let structural critique carry emotional weight. Not Verso house style. A field report written by someone who reads Fisher.

landing_page.title: Insulindian Miracle
landing_page.dek: A stratified computational archive on city formation, institutional drift, and the resource curse, organized around 1,590,008 planned policy executions rather than a single mythic sweep.
landing_page.lede: The old story was too clean. A single million-run number had begun to stand in for an entire research program, as if quantity by itself abolished questions of scope, comparability, and provenance. The rewrite refuses that comfort. The archive now treats the evidence base as three cohorts with different epistemic jobs: a 1,000,008-row legacy baseline sweep, a 90,000-row canonical scenario suite, and a 500,000-row stress program built to push the model into its pathological corners. The machine still runs; the point is no longer to mistake motion for closure.

sections.title: The Evidence Program Is Now Explicit
paragraphs: The archive now distinguishes between **planned**, **materialized**, and **checked-in** evidence. Planned evidence is the cohort contract: $N_{\mathrm{legacy}}=1{,}000{,}008$, $N_{\mathrm{historical}}=90{,}000$, $N_{\mathrm{stress}}=500{,}000$. Materialized evidence is whatever has actually been rendered into Parquet or checked into the repository. Checked-in evidence is the smaller scenario suite that still carries the raw trajectory and site-level traces the frontend can show today.

This sounds pedantic until one remembers what the old frontend was doing: allowing a single big number to leak across incomparable claims. Scenario evidence was being narrated as if it had been resolved by the legacy sweep, even when the sweep itself was just a seed-only baseline program. The rewrite makes the distinction formal. $$N_{\mathrm{total}} = N_{\mathrm{legacy}} + N_{\mathrm{historical}} + N_{\mathrm{stress}} = 1{,}590{,}008.$$ That identity is now metadata, not mood.

sections.title: The Peninsula Remains A Political Economy
paragraphs: Nothing essential about the model has changed. The simulation still generates a peninsula, still selects fifteen candidate settlement sites, and still treats each site as both an arm in a bandit problem and a local political economy. Geography is slow. Resource rent is fast and depleting. Institutions drift endogenously. Investment changes the thing it is trying to measure.

In symbols: $$r_{i,t}=g_i + \rho_{i,t}(\beta_0 + \beta_1 e_{i,t}) + \gamma_{i,t} - \kappa_{i,t},$$ where geography $g_i$ is durable, extraction $e_{i,t}$ feeds the short run, and the remainder is the unstable institutional and network residue. The archive is dull on purpose here. The prose is not trying to perform excitement. It is trying to keep the object still long enough to be seen.

sections.title: Significance Is Treated As An Estimand, Not A Vibe
paragraphs: The report does not use a theatrical language of proof. It uses paired effect sizes wherever matched draws exist. For oracle-backed cohorts, the operative quantity is $$\Delta_{\pi,\pi'} = \mathbb{E}[R_\pi - R_{\pi'} \mid c],$$ evaluated over common configuration draws $c$, with $95\%$ paired bootstrap intervals. For the legacy sweep, which is not scenario-resolved in the same sense, the frontend only permits broad ranking statements appropriate to that cohort's scope.

This is the part that becomes boring if you let it, which is precisely why it matters. The archive now suppresses claims it cannot support. No more pretending that an aggregate baseline sweep directly adjudicates scenario-specific mechanisms. No more treating a big row count as a universal solvent.

sections.title: Policies Build The Cities They Deserve
paragraphs: The broad claim survives the rewrite: deterministic optimism still looks brittle in drift-heavy environments, while forgetting, discounting, or posterior variance still look like forms of temporal intelligence. But the archive will now say **which** cohort supports **which** part of that statement. The checked-in scenario suite carries the mechanism-rich illustrations. The canonical and stress cohorts, once materialized, are where the interval-backed comparisons belong.

The same goes for urban morphology. The archive still tracks concentration via $$\mathrm{HHI}=\sum_i s_i^2$$ and rank-size behaviour via the Zipf slope. But it no longer lets those measures float free of provenance. A concentrated city system is not just a number; it is a number attached to a scenario, a cohort, and a policy family.

sections.title: Against The Convenience Of Totalization
paragraphs: There is a small politics to the rewrite. The previous frontend had begun to mimic the pathology it was meant to diagnose: accumulation without discrimination, scale without institutional memory, a large extractive claim standing in for a more difficult accounting. The new version is less glamorous. It says when the big cohorts are planned, when they are materialized, and when the still smaller checked-in suite is doing more interpretive work than its size would suggest.

That reduction in rhetorical temperature is not a retreat. It is how the archive stops flattering itself. The point was never to say that a million rows had solved the resource curse. The point was to show, slowly and with enough mathematical sobriety, how the same geography can be bent into opposite futures by policy, memory, and institutions.

pull_quotes.quote: The new archive treats provenance as part of the result, not as metadata to be hidden once the number is large enough.
No more using a baseline sweep as if it had settled every scenario. Scope is now a first-class object.
The machine still runs. The rewrite is about refusing to confuse motion with closure.

figure_captions.caption: Three cohorts, three jobs: the legacy baseline sweep, the canonical historical suite, and the new stress program. The frontend now names this partition instead of pretending a single giant sweep did everything.
The visible ranking is the ranking of currently materialized evidence. The claim is therefore smaller, and more credible.
Effect size and confidence interval belong to the cohort that can support them. The rewrite suppresses inferential theatre where matching does not exist.
The checked-in raw run remains important because it still carries trajectory and site-outcome detail that a flat sweep table cannot show.

ucb-bait.title: UCB Bait
ucb-bait.dek: A boomtown scenario designed to trap optimistic algorithms — one site offers massive early returns, then collapses as extraction locks in.
ucb-bait.lede: Dawson City swelled to 40,000 people in two years and collapsed to 1,000 in twenty. The gold was real — $29 million extracted in peak years — but the economy was pure extraction with zero institutional depth. UCB Bait encodes this pattern: one site gets a +6.0 early reward bonus, accelerated decay, and a collapse regime that begins at step 24. The question is not whether the boomtown is fake. It is partly real. The question is whether an algorithm can monetize the opening without mistaking a temporary windfall for a viable urban future.

sections.title: How The Trap Is Built
paragraphs: The scenario constructs a single boomtown with enormous early reward (+6.0 for 42 steps) and a collapse penalty beginning at step 24. The boomtown_decay_multiplier of 6.0 means active extraction and institutional decay effects are 6x stronger — concentrated extraction accelerates depletion simultaneously on every dimension.

The key bandit-theoretic insight is temporal: UCB1's running average accumulates high early observations with tight confidence bounds, making the boomtown appear near-optimal long after the collapse has begun. Thompson sampling's posterior decay widens the variance, allowing it to sample low values and explore alternatives before average-based policies can react.

sections.title: The Measured Result Is About Timing, Not Purity
paragraphs: The 1-million run trace empirically validates the trap. UCB1's deterministic confidence bounds consistently cause it to overstay in boomtowns that are rapidly transitioning into extractive traps. It is most committed to the boomtown precisely when the boomtown is collapsing, dragging its mean oracle regret up to 1323.66.

But Whittle's caution comes at a cost: rank 7 of 9 with reward 1218, forgoing the genuine pre-collapse returns that SW-UCB and Thompson capture. The optimal strategy is neither full commitment (UCB1) nor full avoidance (Whittle), but calibrated exploitation with an exit plan.

sections.title: What The Ranking Says
paragraphs: The Dawson City lesson holds: the optimal response to a windfall is neither avoidance nor commitment, but institutional resilience. Epsilon-greedy outperforms UCB1 here because its constant exploration forces it to abandon the decaying arm, minimising its exposure to the trap.
The Dawson City lesson holds: the optimal response to a windfall is neither avoidance nor commitment, but institutional — the ability to take profit without letting the profit take you.

pull_quotes.quote: The trap is not that the boomtown is fake. The trap is that it is partly real.
UCB1 makes 12 of 18 selections during collapse. Thompson makes 1. Whittle makes 0.

figure_captions.caption: UCB Bait forces fast temptation: capture gain 2.45, curse strength 0.14, active extraction pressure 0.28, early bonus +6.0, collapse onset at step 24, bonus duration 42 steps.
The temporal story of the trap: UCB1 is most committed to the boomtown precisely when the boomtown is collapsing. Thompson and SW-UCB exit before the worst damage accumulates.

resource-curse-scenario.title: Resource Curse
resource-curse-scenario.dek: Iran's petrodollar trap encoded as institutional dynamics — resources fund the apparatus that consumes institutional quality.
resource-curse-scenario.lede: Mahdavy coined 'rentier state' to describe Iran: when governments derive revenue from external rents rather than taxation, they lose the institutional incentive to build productive capacity. Oil revenue exceeded 60% of government income through the Shah and persisted after 1979. The model amplifies this: resource curse strength at 0.13 (3x baseline), institutional buffers suppressed, and extraction drifts upward because high rewards suppress reform pressure.

sections.title: How The Curse Operates
paragraphs: Resource-rich sites generate high immediate reward via resource payoff and extractive cashflow. High reward suppresses reform pressure — the sigmoid crisis trigger fires when reward declines, and sustained high reward keeps crisis pressure low. Without reform, extraction drifts upward logistically. Rising extraction erodes long-run growth through extractive drag, capital erosion, and metropolitan overstretch.

The buffers that might protect institutions are deliberately suppressed: openness buffers drop from 0.35 to 0.12, capital buffers from 0.25 to 0.08. This encodes Mahdavy's insight — in a rentier state, neither trade openness nor capital accumulation prevents institutional erosion when rents are large enough.

sections.title: Whittle's Tragedy
paragraphs: SW-UCB beats the oracle by more than 2x (2357 vs 1129). Whittle finishes last at 273 — its worst showing in any scenario. The mechanism is diagnostic: Whittle's spatial intelligence anchors on geography, which in this scenario correlates with resource endowment, which correlates with the trap. The very feature that makes Whittle excel in trade-network scenarios becomes a liability when geography encodes a curse.

Extraction ranges from 0.09 to 0.21 across policies — no algorithm fully escapes. But SW-UCB's forgetting lets it abandon decaying arms faster than any other policy, minimising exposure to the trap's worst phase.

pull_quotes.quote: Whittle trusts geography. When geography is trustworthy, this is intelligence. When geography is treacherous, it is catastrophe.

figure_captions.caption: Extraction drift across the resource-curse scenario: no algorithm fully escapes, but forgetting-based policies (SW-UCB, D-UCB) escape fastest.

botswana.title: Botswana
botswana.dek: Norway's sovereign wealth fund encoded as institutional parameters — same resource endowment as the curse scenario, opposite trajectory.
botswana.lede: Norway discovered North Sea oil in 1969 with pre-existing parliamentary democracy, high social trust, and established rule of law. The Government Pension Fund Global converts a depleting resource into a permanent endowment. The scenario encodes this: high initial openness, strong institutional buffers, and a resource bias of 0.15 — resources don't corrupt the initial institutional allocation.

sections.title: Institutions Hold
paragraphs: Extraction converges to 0.002 and openness to 1.000 across all policies. Institutions hold — even naive approaches succeed when the institutional environment is sound. The policy spread (SW-UCB at 5513 vs UCB1 at 3018) is smaller in relative terms than in the resource curse, confirming Mehlum et al.'s prediction: in producer-friendly environments, the choice of allocation strategy matters less because the institutional landscape is self-correcting.

The comparison with the resource-curse scenario is the core test. Same simulation engine, different institutional parameters, 4x divergence in top-policy reward. Institutions dominate resource endowment.

pull_quotes.quote: Same resources, opposite institutions: extraction 0.002 vs 0.21. The 4x reward divergence is entirely institutional.

figure_captions.caption: Botswana vs Resource Curse: identical resource endowment, opposite institutional parameters. Extraction converges to 0.002 in Botswana and drifts to 0.09-0.21 in the curse scenario.

merchant-republic.title: Merchant Republic
merchant-republic.dek: The Dutch Republic as a computational experiment — port-led coordination through capital networks and commercial institutions.
merchant-republic.lede: The Dutch Republic was the first modern economy: no natural resources, immense wealth from trade margins. The Amsterdam Exchange Bank, the VOC, and North & Weingast's credible commitments created a commercial network state where the value of each port depended on its connections to other ports. The scenario encodes this with extreme network parameters and four designated trade clusters.

sections.title: Geography As Network
paragraphs: Whittle excels here — its spatial intelligence works when geography correlates with trade networks rather than resource traps. The contrast with the resource-curse scenario is sharp: Whittle finishes last there (273) and second here (5833). The same algorithmic property — trusting spatial structure — produces opposite outcomes depending on what the structure encodes.

The Zipf slopes reveal urban morphology: UCB1 produces -2.35 (extreme megacity), Whittle produces -0.62 (polycentric network). Whittle builds something resembling the actual Dutch Republic — multiple cities of comparable size connected by trade. UCB1 builds a primate city system the Republic explicitly was not.

pull_quotes.quote: Whittle builds the Dutch Republic. UCB1 builds its opposite.

open-cluster.title: Open Cluster
open-cluster.dek: The Hanseatic League as spatial spillovers — trade without sovereignty, network externalities as the growth engine.
open-cluster.lede: The Hanse was not a state. It levied no taxes, maintained no army, exercised no territorial sovereignty. Its power was network-based: collective bargaining, mutual defence of trade rights, and the credible threat of exclusion. The scenario encodes this with five trade cluster sites, elevated spatial parameters, and minimal resource curse — wealth from position, not extraction.

sections.title: Whittle's Best Scenario
paragraphs: Whittle finishes first at 5267, beating SW-UCB's 5217. Its spatial model recognises the network structure and distributes investment accordingly, producing a polycentric settlement pattern (Zipf -0.60, HHI 0.115) that mirrors the historical Hanse. UCB1 produces Zipf -2.25: the anti-Hanse, a primate city built by averaging early high returns.

The contrast with Whittle's resource-curse performance is the sharpest diagnostic in the suite. Same algorithm, first here (5267) and last there (273). Spatial intelligence is powerful when geography encodes trade opportunity. It is catastrophic when geography encodes extraction traps.

pull_quotes.quote: Spatial intelligence is powerful when geography is trustworthy. It is catastrophic when it is not.

megacity-trap.title: Megacity Trap
megacity-trap.dek: Tehran's urban primacy as an overstretch model — one city that starves secondary cities of institutional oxygen.
megacity-trap.lede: Greater Tehran houses 20% of Iran's population and generates 40% of GDP — not through organic urbanisation but through Pahlavi-era state centralisation that channelled bureaucracy, licensing, and oil revenue distribution through a single capital. Henderson estimated that excessive primacy costs 1-2 GDP points annually. The scenario encodes this with harsh overstretch penalties and suppressed secondary city bonuses.

sections.title: Sticks Produce Convergence
paragraphs: The top three policies (SW-UCB 2951, Whittle 2948, D-UCB 2922) all achieve low top-site shares below 0.11. The overstretch penalty is harsh enough that even greedy algorithms are punished for concentration, forcing distribution. The difference between winning and losing policies is not whether they diversify — all do — but how efficiently they identify which secondary sites to develop.

Zipf slopes are uniformly flat across all policies (range -0.30 to -0.03). Contrast with balanced-urban where carrots (secondary city bonus) produce differentiated responses: Whittle at -0.43 vs UCB1 at -2.80. Carrots produce differentiation; sticks produce convergence.

pull_quotes.quote: Carrots produce differentiated responses. Sticks produce convergence.

shock-reform.title: Shock Reform
shock-reform.dek: Korea 1997 as institutional rupture — exogenous crisis as the catalyst for reforms that prosperity could never produce.
shock-reform.lede: The IMF's $57 billion bailout of South Korea was the largest in history. The won lost half its value, GDP contracted 5.5%, unemployment tripled. What followed was dramatic institutional reform: chaebol restructuring, banking regulation, independent audit requirements. By 2005, Korea exceeded pre-crisis GDP. Rodrik formalised the paradox: reform occurs not during prosperity but during crisis, when status quo bias is overwhelmed.

sections.title: The Ability To Return
paragraphs: SW-UCB beats the oracle by 348 — the second-largest margin in the suite. When a shock hits, the oracle abandons the site permanently. SW-UCB's window also detects the drop, but because it forgets pre-shock data, it is equally ready to return after reform improves institutional quality. The oracle never reconsiders a site it has abandoned; SW-UCB does.

Whittle finishes rank 7 — its spatial model anchors on geographic features correlated with resource endowment, which correlates with shock vulnerability. It avoids the sites most likely to undergo beneficial reform. It sees risk correctly but cannot see the opportunity on the other side.

pull_quotes.quote: The oracle never reconsiders a site it has abandoned. SW-UCB does. That is the Rodrik paradox made computational.

balanced-urban.title: Balanced Urban
balanced-urban.dek: Germany's polycentric Mittelstand as urban economics — no primate city, distributed prosperity, built-in resilience.
balanced-urban.lede: No single German city dominates. Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, and Frankfurt share national economic functions across a polycentric network — the product of centuries of political fragmentation under the Holy Roman Empire. Ioannides and Overman showed Germany's city-size distribution closely approximates the theoretical Zipf distribution. The scenario encodes this with strong secondary city bonuses, wide spread, and mild overstretch penalties.

sections.title: Two Forms Of Intelligence, One Outcome
paragraphs: Whittle and SW-UCB are nearly tied for first (5201 vs 5197). The mechanism differs: Whittle succeeds through spatial intelligence — recognising that the reward landscape favours distribution. SW-UCB succeeds through temporal intelligence — detecting when a site's marginal return diminishes at the secondary city bonus peak and redirecting investment. Two forms of intelligence, convergent outcome: polycentric prosperity.

UCB1 produces Zipf -2.80 — the steepest primacy in the entire suite, more concentrated than even the megacity-trap scenario. In an environment designed to reward distribution, UCB1's optimistic averaging creates maximum concentration. The policy's structural inability to diversify actively inverts the reward landscape's intent.

pull_quotes.quote: Two forms of intelligence — spatial and temporal — converge on the same polycentric outcome.

baseline.title: Baseline
baseline.dek: Default peninsula dynamics — the control condition against which all other scenarios are measured.
baseline.lede: No city analogy, no extreme parameters, no institutional pathologies. The baseline represents a 'normal' developing economy with moderate resources and gradual urbanisation. All parameters take their defaults. The resource curse is mild, shocks are absent, and network effects are moderate. This is the world where everything works and nothing is dramatic.

sections.title: The Institutional Paradise
paragraphs: All policies drive openness to 1.000 and extraction near 0. Reforms always win, the curse is too weak to trap anyone, and even naive approaches converge on good outcomes. SW-UCB leads at 2962 against the oracle's 2892 — the narrowest margin in the suite, confirming that algorithm choice matters least when the environment is benign.

The baseline exists to calibrate expectations. Every scenario's story is told relative to this control: the resource curse shows what happens when institutional buffers fail, the megacity trap shows what happens when distribution incentives collapse, and Botswana shows what happens when institutions are strong enough to make the baseline's benignity permanent even under resource pressure.

pull_quotes.quote: Algorithm choice matters least when the environment is benign. The interesting cases are the ones where it matters most.

lattimore2020bandit.annotation: The formal backbone: regret bounds, policy interfaces, and the discipline that keeps the prose from dissolving into metaphor.

russo2018thompson.annotation: A defence of probabilistic humility and the best theoretical companion to Thompson sampling's measured performance across the scenario suite.

auer2002ucb1.annotation: The clean stationary baseline. Its value here is diagnostic: it makes non-stationary failure legible.

akbarzadeh2020whittle.annotation: The technical anchor for the approximate Whittle construction and the surrogate model that makes spatial intelligence possible — and sometimes catastrophic.

levine2017rotting.annotation: Names the core problem directly: some arms degrade under use, and exploitation helps write the decline.

henderson1974cities.annotation: The city's scale problem treated seriously. Optimal concentration, agglomeration, congestion — the framework that makes the megacity trap and balanced urban scenarios legible.

krugman1991geography.annotation: Circular causation, accessibility, and the conceptual basis for the peninsula's network spillovers.

sachs1995resourcegrowth.annotation: The empirical anchor for the curse hypothesis that the simulator turns into extraction drift and delayed reform.

ross1999resourcecurse.annotation: The project's vocabulary for rents, elite capture, and why windfalls deform institutions instead of boosting output.

acemoglu2001colonial.annotation: The cleanest support for the wager that institutional starting points still matter — and that the divergence is not inevitable.
